headline: Salience Labs, which builds light-based network switches for AI data centers, has raised $125 million from investors including Intel Capital and AMD Ventures.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: useful chip-industry backing, but the product is not yet in volume production.
importance_line: Data center operators may get faster and less power-hungry networks, but the claims of a world-first switch are the company's own and mass production is still ahead.
summary: SiliconANGLE reports that Salience Labs raised $125 million in a Series B round led by Bullhound Capital, with Intel Capital and AMD Ventures among the investors. The startup makes switches that move data between AI computers using light only, which it says cuts delay and power use, and it will spend the money on manufacturing and on larger switches after showing a 64-port model, a claim that comes from the company.
notes: default_v1 MKT; ENE chosen because the story is about data center networking hardware.
